title: DMP4NFDI Outreach Support Concept
desc: The DMP4NFDI Outreach Support Concept defines a framework for supporting NFDI consortia in promoting data and software management services and fostering their adoption within their research communities. It outlines the support options provided by DMP4NFDI and the rationale for their implementation, building on previous collaborations and ongoing exchange with NFDI consortia. The concept follows a needs-based approach and uses short-term incubator projects as the primary mechanism for targeted outreach support. The measures include community engagement, needs assessment, capacity building, cross-consortium collaboration, and broader outreach activities to facilitate the onboarding of interested consortia. Together, these measures provide flexible support that can be adapted to the specific requirements and contexts of NFDI consortia. This publication covers deliverable 2.1, "Concept for outreach support," of the  DMP4NFDI integration phase proposal .

title: README Template for Research Datasets in CRC 1615 SMART Reactors
desc: This document provides a README template for documenting research datasets produced within CRC 1615 “SMART Reactors for Future Process Engineering.” It supports researchers in describing dataset context, methodological information, file structure, access conditions, licensing, reproducibility requirements, ethical and legal aspects, versioning, and contact information. The template is part of a broader set of research data management documents developed for CRC 1615. It complements the Research Data Management Plan Handbook by translating its guidance into a practical dataset-level documentation structure. Together, these documents support consistent documentation, organization, preservation, and publication of research data in alignment with the FAIR principles and the research data management requirements of the German Research Foundation (DFG). The template is intended for use when preparing datasets for repository publication, including publication via TORE, Zenodo, or other suitable repositories. It can be adapted to specific subprojects, disciplines, data types, and publication contexts within CRC 1615.

title: Information Sheet: Publishing Research Software as a FAIR Research Output
desc: This information sheet provides practical guidance for publishing research software as a FAIR research output within the DFG Collaborative Research Centre (CRC) 1615 SMART Reactors for Future Process Engineering at Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH). It supports researchers in managing software according to FAIR4RS principles and DFG recommendations throughout the research lifecycle. The guide covers software planning, licensing, version control, citation metadata, repository selection, DOI assignment, software archiving, and linking software with datasets and publications. It also includes a recommended publication workflow, quality assurance checklist, repository structure, guidance for special cases such as AI-generated code, and best practices for ensuring reproducibility and long-term reuse. The document is intended for researchers, PhD students, and project teams developing scripts, workflows, simulation models, analysis pipelines, notebooks, or software packages and should be used alongside the CRC 1615 Research Data Management Handbook, RDMP Template, and README Template for dataset publications to support standardized, FAIR, and reproducible research practices across all CRC subprojects.

title: CRC 1615 Research Data Management Plan (RDMP) Template
desc: This Research Data Management Plan (RDMP) Template was developed for the DFG Collaborative Research Centre (CRC) 1615 SMART Reactors for Future Process Engineering at Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH). It provides a standardized framework for documenting project-specific research data management practices throughout the research lifecycle in accordance with the FAIR principles and the German Research Foundation (DFG) guidelines. The template supports researchers in planning, documenting, storing, backing up, describing, sharing, preserving, and publishing research data in a consistent and reproducible manner. It covers key aspects including data types, metadata standards, software and code, documentation, quality assurance, storage and backup, repository selection, legal obligations, versioning, publication strategies, and responsibilities. The template is intended to facilitate the preparation of project-specific Research Data Management Plans across all CRC 1615 subprojects and should be used together with the accompanying Research Data Management Plan Handbook , README Template , and other CRC 1615 RDM guidance documents to promote FAIR, transparent, and sustainable research data management.

title: CRC 1615 Research Data Management Plan Handbook
desc: This handbook provides comprehensive guidance for developing, maintaining, and publishing Research Data Management Plans (RDMPs) within the DFG Collaborative Research Centre (CRC) 1615 SMART Reactors for Future Process Engineering at Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH). It supports researchers in implementing FAIR data principles, complying with DFG requirements, and establishing good research data management practices throughout the research lifecycle. The handbook covers data planning, documentation, metadata, storage, quality assurance, legal aspects, repository selection, internal and external data exchange, and long-term preservation. It also defines the CRC 1615 RDM workflow, including the use of TUHH DataPlan for RDMP creation and TORE for RDMP publication, and provides practical recommendations for publishing datasets, software, and metadata. The handbook is intended to be used together with the CRC 1615 RDMP Template, README Template, and Research Software Publication Sheet to support standardized, FAIR, and reproducible research across all CRC subprojects. The document is versioned and will be updated as RDM practices, institutional infrastructure, and funder requirements evolve.

title: Research Data Management - A Practical Introduction
desc: The motivation for this best practice manual for research data management (RDM) resulted from many discussions and interviews that we conducted with users from the engineering and natural sciences communities. It became clear again and again that a practice-oriented guide for real research data management is missing and urgently needed. The available, more theoretically oriented presentations are generally only of limited help in practical application. For example, they do not explain how to specifically write a data management plan (DMP) and what third-party funding bodies look out for. Even for the practical operation of an electronic laboratory notebook (ELN), users are almost exclusively dependent on the manuals of the respective system, which represents a major hurdle for many users. Legal issues are also often a problem, for example when it comes to granting licenses or using external data. We have therefore decided to write this best practice handbook for RDM in order to close these gaps and provide free practical help for scientists. For example, we go into detail about how to write a DMP, explain the legal aspects of RDM that need to be taken into account in everyday life, show examples of how to use and operate the open-source electronic lab note-books JuliaBase, eLabFTW and Kadi4Mat, discuss aspects of data quality and analysis and which open-source software can be used for this purpose. We show how data can be exchanged and tracked between different ELNs and we demonstrate the publication of data. We also explain how research data can be used and reused for machine learning and what requirements must be met for this. title: Standardising Data Management Plans for Machine-Actionable Data Management across NFDI and beyond
desc: Abstract Achieving FAIRness of research data implies the application of best practices and machine-actionable metadata. Data management plans (DMPs) as a starting point for research data management activities can support both, when implemented as machine-actionable DMPs (maDMP) [1]. Machine-actionable DMP templates and tools adapted for community-specific needs communicate best practices and standardised workflows, provide up-to-date information on service offers, and connect all stakeholders involved in the RDM process. In order to achieve this interconnection, a standard for DMP templates is needed that consortia and services can rely upon. The NFDI basic service in development DMP4NFDI works towards this goal by developing a NFDI-wide standard for DMPs, the NFDI DMP Template Framework, and providing a common tool connecting consortia and their RDM services: RDMO. DMP4NFDI is based on the work of the cross-consortia working group infra-dmp in NFDI section Common Infrastructures, and the vision developed in its workshops and discussions [2].  We base our standard development on two principles: 1) ensuring interoperability across NFDI consortia as a prerequisite for metadata exchange and cross-consortia solutions, 2) allowing community-specific adaptations when needed. As a starting point, the de facto standard for maDMPs developed and maintained by the RDA “DMP Common Standards” working group [1] was chosen, as it ensures international interoperability. This standard is already supported by RDMO, the DMP tool most used in Germany. We derive a cross-consortia standard for DMP templates by thoroughly mapping questions currently used in DMP templates. title: Template for the NFDI4Biodiversity & iDiv Seasonal School on Data Management in Ecology and Environmental Science 2024
desc: This document describes a one-week course program for a Seasonal School on research data management (RDM) from 2024 which was organised for the second time by partners from the NFDI4Biodiversity consortium. The course aimed to provide young scientists in ecology and environmental science with state-of-the-art skills and knowledge in handling scientific data throughout the data life cycle. Lectures and practical sessions were given by experts from renowned universities, data centers, and research institutions in the environmental research community, covering general aspects of RDM and aspects specifically important for handling ecological data. The participants were introduced to Jupyter notebooks and learned how to combine software tools like Jupyter, R, GitHub, spreadsheet tools, and NFDI4Biodiversity Tools and Services. The course was conducted remotely and targeted PhD students (R1). This publication summarises detailed information about the structure, organisation, and lessons learned, and is supposed to be used as a guide for similar events. We list all course materials (presentation slides, video recordings, code, Jupyter notebooks, trainings data sets) and accounts required to follow the course program in your own pace. Additional code and training data sets are available here:  https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15594632 . The course requires a minimum of programming skills in R (Python is optional).

title: Identification of core elements for a machine-actionable Data Management Plan metadata schema in the NFDI
desc: From 28 to 30 October 2024,  ZB MED Information Centre for Life Sciences organized a hackathon in Cologne within the scope of NFDI4DataScience with the purpose of identifying core elements for a machine-actionable Data Managemnt Plan (maDMP) across the German National Research Data Infrastructure (NFDI). We used as starting/reference point the  maDMP application profile from the Research Data Alliance DMP Commons Working Group . Here we report on the activities and findings. The dataset corresponding to crosswalks can be found at DOI:10.5281/zenodo.15129830 Abstract: The interoperability of data management plans (DMPs) across platforms and application profiles plays a key role in the implementation of good scientific practice and of the FAIR data principles. The application profile for "machine-actionable DMPs" published by the Research Data Alliance (RDA) marks an important step in this direction. More recently, networking initiatives such as the German National Research Data Infrastructure (NFDI) are collecting and generating templates for DMPs based on the needs of different subject-related communities and implemented in different DMP software tools. In a two-day hackathon we analyzed the RDA maDMP application profile, discussed the meaning and applicability of the proposed elements and aligned them to selected community-driven schemas and platforms for DMPs and for metadata. The results are available in the form of crosswalks and are intended to pave the way towards an maDMP based on schema.org to improve information exchange between DMP platforms and other research data services, and alignment between DMPs and Software Management Plans. title: Infra-dmp und DMP4NFDI - Datenmanagementpläne in der NFDI
desc: Abstract Jürgen Windeck, Daniela Hausen, Katja Diederichs, Marisabel Gonzalez Ocanto, Sabine Schönau, David Wallace Daten-  (DMPs) und Softwaremanagementpläne (SMPs) gehören zu den zentralen Aspekten im Forschungsdatenmanagement und werden in nahezu allen NFDI-Konsortien thematisiert. Um das Thema voranzutreiben, Erfahrungs- und Entwicklungsaustausch sowie Synergien zwischen den Konsortien zu fördern, wurde 2022 die Arbeitsgruppe infra-dmp gegründet (Enke et al. 2023), die konsortienübergreifend agiert und die Themen in der NFDI-Section Common Infrastructures einbringt.  Für die Kommunikation und Arbeit innerhalb infra-dmp wurden regelmäßige Quartalstreffen und Ad-hoc-Arbeitsgruppen etabliert (Hausen & Windeck 2023). Hier werden z.B. Erfahrungen über die Entwicklung von DMP-Templates geteilt, DMP-Tools abgestimmt, Herausforderungen diskutiert und gemeinsame Lösungen und Herangehensweisen entwickelt. Letzteres spiegelt sich in der Arbeit der Ad-hoc-Gruppen wider. Diese bearbeiten Themen wie übergreifende Qualitätskriterien für Templates (Krause et al. 2024), die Entwicklung einer Vision für DMPs in der NFDI (vgl. Diederichs et al. 2024) oder organisieren Workshops rund um das Thema DMP und SMP. Infra-dmp tauscht sich außerdem auch mit anderen nationalen Initiativen aus, wie z.B. DINI-Arbeitsgruppen oder der RDMO Community.  Aus einer Ad-hoc-Arbeitsgruppe ist ebenfalls der NFDI Basisdienst DMP4NFDI hervorgegangen. Dieser unterstützt NFDI-Konsortien bei der Bereitstellung von Services für DMPs und basiert auf den Bedarfen und Zielen der Konsortien für DMPs und SMPs in der NFDI. title: DMP4NFDI - A Central Service for Data/Software Management Plans
desc: DMP4NFDI - Ein Basisdienst für Datenmanagementpläne in der NFDI  Datenmanagementpläne (DMPs) und Softwaremanagementpläne (SMPs) sind zentrale Elemente im Forschungsdatenmanagement. Im Sommer 2024 startete der Basisdienst DMP4NFDI, um diese Themen gezielt für die Konsortien der Nationalen Forschungsdateninfrastruktur (NFDI) zu adressieren.  Der Basisdient DMP4NFDI baut eine zentrale Infrastruktur für DMPs und SMPs in der NFDI auf. Das Hauptziel ist die Unterstützung der NFDI-Konsortien bei der Entwicklung und Bereitstellung standardisierter DMP-Services.  Die Konzeption des Basisdienstes basiert auf Erkenntnissen der NFDI-Arbeitsgruppe infra-dmp, die innerhalb der NFDI-Sektion Common Infrastructures angesiedelt ist. Diese Arbeitsgruppe fördert den konsortienübergreifenden Austausch über die Nutzung und Weiterentwicklung von DMPs und erarbeitete u.a. eine Vision für DMPs, die spezifische Bedarfe für den Basisdienst aufzeigte.  In der Initialisierungsphase entwickelt der Dienst gemeinsam mit Pilot-Konsortien das NFDI DMP Template Framework, das sich am de-facto Standard für machine-actionable DMPs orientiert und die Erstellung interoperabler und standardisierter Templates ermöglichen soll. Als technische Grundlage dient eine mandantenfähige RDMO-Instanz, die den NFDI-Konsortien eigene anpassbare Mandanten von RDMO bereitstellt, in der sie gleichzeitig von einer zentralen Infrastruktur profitieren können. title: Collecting DMP Requirements for NFDI - Report on DMP4NFDI activities
desc: DMP4NFDI is the basic service in development for data management planning within NFDI. The service supports NFDI consortia providing services for data management plans (DMPs), software management plans (SMPs) or analogues. It offers RDMO hosting, support & training for consortia staff and develops and maintains the NFDI DMP Template Framework to facilitate template development and interoperability, and it supports consortia to integrate DMPs, SMPs etc. with their service portfolio. During the initial development phase (June 2024 - May 2025), we are collecting requirements for DMP and SMP services in the NFDI by organising workshops and exchanges with the consortia and the general RDM community. This report summarizes our results after three workshops, participation in two hackathons, presenting the service at several occasions and exchange with consortia in infra-dmp and individual meetings.

desc: Vortrag im Rahmen der NFDI4Culture-Workshopreihe  "In vier Schritten zu mehr Nachhaltigkeit. Datenqualitäts-Strategien für Museen und Sammlungen" (Workshop 2: Sinnvolles Management für bessere Datenqualität. Schwerpunkt Datenmanagementpläne ), 23.6.2023 (online) Die Präsentation nähert sich dem Thema Management auf drei Ebenen: Institution, Projekt, Daten. Im Fokus stehen Datenmanagementpläne (DMP), die als Schlüsselelemente eines guten Datenmanagements gelten. Dabei werden auch die Anforderungen skizziert, denen Sammlungsdaten heute gerecht werden müssen.

title: NFDI4Microbiota Data Management Plan (DMP) Template
desc: This document is meant as a draft for DMPs that should be filled out by every research project hosted on the NFDI4Microbiota platform that is officially supported by NFDI4Microbiota data stewards (e.g. for partners and use cases, link to helpdesk for NFDI4Microbiota flagged DMPs). DMPs should optimally be filled out before projects are submitted for funding and are supposed to produce the „Research Data Handling“ chapter of proposals as required by e.g. DFG . The DMP should be extended and updated after funding is secured and can be referred to in future analysis or support processes. We could try to make this mandatory for use cases and similar projects within NFDI4Microbiota. Optimally, this reduces researchers efforts in the planning phase and enables them to assure adequate data handling during the realization phase. For any NFDI4Microbiota related project this could serve as a best practice example.

title: NFDI-MatWerk Guide: Research Data Management Plan
desc: The document (RDMP-Guide) gives insights into a structured framework for researchers (specific for materials science community) to efficiently handle data throughout a project. It outlines best practices for data collection, storage, documentation, sharing, and preservation. The guide helps ensure data integrity, compliance with legal and ethical standards, and enhances the transparency and reproducibility of research findings.

title: Introduction to NFDI4Biodiversity, the eResearch Center of Marburg University, and their tools and services
desc: In this talk, Juliane Röder gives a quick overview of the tools and services of the NFDI4Biodiversity consortium and the local eResearch Center of the Philipps University of Marburg, with a focus on training resources. The eResearch Center provides generic tools and services along the full data life cycle in close collaboration with the Hessian Research Data Infrastructures (HeFDI) . NFDI4Biodiversity provides a large range of discipline specific tools and services for reseachers working with biodiversity data. For further details on the projects, feel free to take a look at the available  training resources as well as information on the HeFDI initiative and the eResearch Center of the University of Marburg.

title: Recommendations for Using Data Management Plans in Academic Research Data Management Training
desc: General Information: This paper was presented at the 2023 Hochschuldidaktik Informatik (HDI) conference on 13-14 September 2023 in Aachen, Germany. It is published in the conference proceedings, which can be accessed via this link: https://delfi-tagung.de/fileadmin/FG/BBI/user_upload/6400_HDI_2023_-_Tagungsband_-_Broschuere_-_Innenseiten_-_DIN_A4_-_RZ_WEB.pdf [accessed on 2023-Dec-04]. Abstract:   In this report, we share our experiences using data management plans (DMP) for the academic teaching of research data management (RDM). We present concepts to train students in a university lecture over a semester and to train researchers in an interdisciplinary collaborative research center in shorter workshop formats. Based on our observations, we provide recommendations for future DMP-based mediations of competencies in handling research data. These recommendations include imparting basic RDM knowledge before building capacities in creating DMPs, establishing feedback loops to evaluate DMPs, and relying on a printed DMP rather than an IT platform when training time is limited.

title: FAIRmat, Guide to Writing a Research Data Management Plan
desc: In this guide, we will provide you with comprehensive information and practical tips specific to the fields of condensed-matter physics and materials science on creating a data management plan (DMP) that meets the DFG requirements and aligns your research with the FAIR data principles, the DFG code of conduct, and the EU open science policy. We will take you through the essential components of a DMP, provide tips on data management best practices, and offer guidance on appropriate tools and technologies. By the end of this guide, you will have the knowledge and tools necessary to create a thorough and effective DMP that not only meets the requirements of the DFG but also supports the long-term success of your research project. This guide follows the sections in the DFG checklist, and the questions to be addressed as required by the DFG are listed after each section. Although this guide is based on the requirements of the DFG, the information is not exclusive to any specific funding agency and can be used as a general guide for other research areas. Before preparing a DMP for your project, make sure to check the specific requirements for your funding agency, discipline, and research institution.

title: StoryMachine D1.1 Data Management Plan (Version 1)
desc: This document outlines the data management strategy for the StoryMachine project, a UK–German collaboration funded by AHRC and DFG. It describes how project data will be collected, documented, stored, shared, and preserved according to the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable). The DMP ensures compliance with ethical and legal requirements and provides guidance for sustainable, long-term management of project outputs

title: The Data Management Plan - from a burden to a key success factor
desc: Recently, funding agencies have begun to require sections on research data management in grant applications and the submission of a detailed Data Management Plan (DMP) during the initial phase of a funded research project. These DMPs are set as milestones to be achieved for a successful research project. Scientists often view DMPs as a burden and additional work that distracts them from active research. This is due to different requirements from different funders, lack of established routines for writing DMPs, and lack of tools and services for efficient research data management. We analyzed the DMP guidelines provided by the European Union for its Horizon Europe and ERC (European Research Council) grants, as well as those of the German Research Foundation (DFG). We summarized the requirements and topics to be covered, contrasting similarities and differences while keeping an eye on the different details. This poster will provide an overview of the basics of writing a DMP and will emphasize that writing is only a small part. The main work is preparation, thorough discussion, and decision making about how to manage the data. The groundwork includes documentation and data quality, storage and archiving, legal aspects, data sharing, and accessibility, to name a few. Some funders require researchers to apply the FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Re-usable) data principles for research data management. We will present our hands-on workshop for planning and writing DMPs and provide examples of how NOMAD, a web-based open source service, can support research data management according to the FAIR principles.
